Classic Cornbread Stuffing

Served at: Thanksgiving Day (United States)

Serves 8-10Prep 25 minCook 40 min

Cornbread Stuffing is a beloved staple on many Thanksgiving tables across the United States, offering a delightful Southern twist to the traditional holiday dressing. Its slightly sweet and crumbly texture, combined with savory herbs and vegetables, makes it a comforting and essential side dish that perfectly complements roasted turkey and gravy.

Ingredients

  • 8 cups (about 1.5 lbs or 680g) crumbled day-old cornbread
  • 1 cup (226g) unsalted butter, divided
  • 2 large yellow onions, finely chopped
  • 4 stalks celery, finely chopped
  • 2 cloves garlic, minced
  • 1 tablespoon fresh sage, chopped (or 1 teaspoon dried)
  • 1 tablespoon fresh thyme, chopped (or 1 teaspoon dried)
  • 1 teaspoon salt
  • 1/2 teaspoon black pepper
  • 2 large eggs, lightly beaten
  • 3-4 cups (720-960ml) chicken or vegetable broth, warm

Method

  1. Preheat your oven to 375°F (190°C). Lightly grease a 9x13 inch (23x33 cm) baking dish.
  2. Spread the crumbled cornbread on a large baking sheet and toast in the preheated oven for 10-15 minutes, or until lightly golden and slightly dried out. This helps prevent a soggy stuffing. Remove from oven and set aside.
  3. In a large skillet or Dutch oven, melt 1/2 cup (113g) of the butter over medium heat. Add the chopped onions and celery and cook, stirring occasionally, until softened, about 8-10 minutes.
  4. Add the minced garlic, fresh sage, and fresh thyme to the skillet. Cook for another 2 minutes until fragrant.
  5. In a large mixing bowl, combine the toasted cornbread crumbs, the sautéed onion and celery mixture, salt, and pepper. Toss gently to combine.
  6. In a separate small bowl, whisk the eggs. Pour the beaten eggs over the cornbread mixture and mix well.
  7. Gradually add 3 cups (720ml) of the warm broth to the cornbread mixture, stirring until just moistened. The mixture should be moist but not soupy. Add more broth, a little at a time, if it seems too dry.
  8. Melt the remaining 1/2 cup (113g) of butter. Pour half of it into the cornbread mixture and stir gently to incorporate.
  9. Transfer the stuffing mixture to the prepared baking dish. Drizzle the remaining melted butter over the top.
  10. Bake for 30-40 minutes, or until the top is golden brown and the stuffing is heated through and slightly crisp on top. If the top browns too quickly, you can loosely cover it with foil.

Tips

  • For extra flavor, sauté 1/2 pound (225g) of crumbled breakfast sausage or diced mushrooms with the onions and celery.
  • Add 1/2 cup (60g) of chopped pecans or dried cranberries to the mixture for added texture and a touch of sweetness.
  • Prepare the cornbread a day or two in advance to ensure it's stale enough for the best stuffing texture.
